WETREP applies to every kind of oil tanker of more than 600 tonnes deadweight carrying heavy crude oil, heavy fuel oil or bitumen and tar (MSC.190(79) annex para 1.1): tanker-specific. Its north-eastern limit is the straight line from point 19 (51 22'25"N 003 21'52".5E) to point 20 (52 12'N UK east coast, about 001 37'E), confirmed on the chartlet (P-S5). Testing the Circ.67 positions (P-S1) against that line: all south-western and central positions (79, 80, 83, 84, 86) are 25-56' of longitude inside; the north-eastern corner positions (81, 82, 85, 87) lie within about 1-2' of the line (on it within plotting precision). Effectively the whole scheme is inside WETREP, with the NE extremity on the boundary. Outside CALDOVREP (P-S19).

MASTREP area is the Australian SRR for which RCC Australia is responsible (V-S16); the TSS lies in Australian coastal waters well inside the SRR. Mandatory only for foreign vessels between first arrival at and final departure from an Australian port, and for regulated Australian vessels in the MASTREP area (V-S15), so through-transiting foreign ships are outside it. Automatic AIS-based reporting. Pass 4: Marine Order 63 (2019) gives effect to SOLAS V/11 (s.2), applies to regulated Australian vessels and to foreign vessels from arrival at their first Australian port until departure from their final Australian port (s.6(1)), with a strict-liability penalty (s.7). Counted as MRS under the project rule that a national scheme counts when it imposes a penal reporting duty on foreign ships in the TSS under defined voyage conditions. Through traffic not calling at Australian ports is not covered.
